powertrain.firstCheck: From a safe parked position, note whether the warning is steady or flashing and whether the vehicle has rough running, power loss, overheating or another urgent warning.
safety: A flashing engine warning needs prompt attention. Avoid continued driving when the vehicle runs badly; follow its owner manual and arrange assistance.
Stop safely for overheating, a red stop warning, smoke, fuel smell or loss of control. Do not run an engine in an enclosed space.

steps.title: Keep the complete scan report
steps.body: Record the code exactly, including any suffix, module name and current, pending or history status. Save freeze-frame information if your scanner provides it. Do not erase the evidence just to see whether the warning returns.

steps.title: Match the vehicle and the situation
steps.body: Write down the model year, engine or powertrain, symptoms and conditions when the warning appeared. Include recent repairs, battery work or a refueling event as observations, not assumed causes.

steps.title: Use the applicable diagnostic procedure
steps.body: Give the report to a qualified technician or manufacturer service department. The next test depends on the vehicle configuration, other codes and the module that reported the fault.

nextSteps: Request the manufacturer diagnostic path for the complete code and vehicle.
Ask what measurement supports a proposed repair and how the repair will be verified.
limitations: A stored code identifies a reported condition. It does not, by itself, identify a failed part or establish that the vehicle is safe to drive.
Confirm the full code, reporting module, vehicle identification and manufacturer service information. A generic definition is not proof that every vehicle supports this code.
The checks here preserve useful observations. They are not component tests, a repair procedure or a substitute for model-specific diagnosis.

body.firstCheck: Record the warning, affected feature and reporting module. A body-system code may need a scanner that can communicate with that specific module.
body.urgencyLabel: Check the affected safety or convenience system
safety: Do not probe airbag or seat-belt pretensioner wiring, disconnect safety devices, or use a generic code description to decide that restraints are working.
If a safety-system warning is present, follow the exact vehicle manual and arrange qualified service.

chassis.firstCheck: Note the brake, steering, stability or suspension warning shown with the code. A code number alone cannot establish whether braking or steering remains available.
chassis.urgencyLabel: Assess braking and steering warnings first
safety: Stop safely if braking or steering feels abnormal or a red stop/brake warning calls for stopping. Arrange assistance rather than a diagnostic road test.
Do not work beneath an unsupported vehicle or bypass a chassis safety function.

network.firstCheck: Save which modules can be reached and which communication codes each module reports. Record a recent flat battery or repair if one actually occurred.
safety: A communication code is not proof that the named module needs replacement.
Do not bridge diagnostic pins, change module coding or disconnect high-voltage equipment using this reference. Stop safely if a critical vehicle function is affected.

P0300.summary: P0300 is the generic reference for random or multiple-cylinder misfire detection. The warning behavior and other stored codes determine the next diagnostic step.
P0300.meaning: The reported condition is misfire across an unspecified or changing cylinder pattern. This result does not identify an ignition coil, injector or mechanical cause.
P0300.firstCheck: Check whether the engine warning is flashing and whether the vehicle is shaking or losing power. Park safely and arrange prompt assistance when those symptoms are present.
P0300.urgencyLabel: Prioritize rough running or a flashing warning
nextSteps: Keep any cylinder-specific misfire codes with P0300.
Provide cold-start, idle, load and temperature observations to the technician.

P0301.summary: The generic definition identifies misfire detected for cylinder 1. It does not specify which component caused the misfire.
P0301.meaning: The cylinder number belongs to the engine manufacturer’s cylinder numbering. Confirm that layout for the exact engine before interpreting a physical location.
P0301.firstCheck: Record rough running and whether the engine warning flashes. Do not keep running a badly misfiring engine to reproduce the code.
nextSteps: Keep the complete set of misfire and mixture codes.
Ask the workshop to verify the engine-specific cylinder location and diagnostic evidence before replacement.

P0420.summary: P0420 identifies a catalyst-efficiency result below the calibrated threshold for bank 1. It is a monitor result, not a replacement instruction.
P0420.meaning: The complete diagnostic context matters: other engine faults, sensor data and the manufacturer’s monitor criteria must be considered before choosing a repair.
P0420.firstCheck: Save this code with any misfire, mixture or sensor codes. Note whether the warning is steady or flashing and whether the engine is running normally.
nextSteps: Ask which tests distinguish the reported monitor result from its cause.
Confirm the applicable bank and vehicle-specific procedure before authorizing catalyst or sensor replacement.

P0430.summary: P0430 identifies a catalyst-efficiency result below the calibrated threshold for bank 2. It is a monitor result, not a replacement instruction.
P0430.meaning: The complete diagnostic context matters: other engine faults, sensor data and the manufacturer’s monitor criteria must be considered before choosing a repair.
P0430.firstCheck: Save this code with any misfire, mixture or sensor codes. Note whether the warning is steady or flashing and whether the engine is running normally.
nextSteps: Ask which tests distinguish the reported monitor result from its cause.
Confirm the applicable bank and vehicle-specific procedure before authorizing catalyst or sensor replacement.

P0171.summary: The generic definition for P0171 reports a lean-system condition for bank 1. A code alone cannot distinguish an air, fuel, measurement or other underlying fault.
P0171.meaning: Interpret the reported mixture condition alongside the full scan and operating conditions. The engine configuration determines which physical bank the definition refers to.
P0171.firstCheck: Record whether the warning appeared at idle, during acceleration or after a repair. Keep both bank codes if the scanner reports them.
nextSteps: Provide the workshop with the scan’s saved operating conditions.
Request evidence for the repair instead of selecting a part from the code title.

P0455.summary: P0455 reports a large evaporative-emissions leak condition. The code does not identify the leak location.
P0455.meaning: A model with a removable fuel cap has different owner checks from a capless system. Follow the fuel-filler instructions for the actual vehicle.
P0455.firstCheck: With the vehicle parked and engine off, check the normal fuel-cap closure only if the vehicle has a removable cap. Record whether the warning followed refueling.
safety: Keep fuel vapors away from flames, sparks and improvised smoke tests. A noticeable fuel leak or strong fuel smell needs professional assessment.
nextSteps: Use the vehicle’s normal filler instructions; do not force a capless valve.
Arrange proper EVAP diagnosis if the warning persists.

P0456.summary: P0456 reports a very small evaporative-emissions leak condition. The code does not identify the leak location.
P0456.meaning: A model with a removable fuel cap has different owner checks from a capless system. Follow the fuel-filler instructions for the actual vehicle.
P0456.firstCheck: With the vehicle parked and engine off, check the normal fuel-cap closure only if the vehicle has a removable cap. Record whether the warning followed refueling.
safety: Keep fuel vapors away from flames, sparks and improvised smoke tests. A noticeable fuel leak or strong fuel smell needs professional assessment.

P0128.summary: P0128 reports coolant temperature below the thermostat-regulating temperature expected by the diagnostic monitor.
P0128.meaning: This temperature result is not, by itself, proof that the thermostat is the failed part. Vehicle operating data and the manufacturer procedure are needed.
P0128.firstCheck: Record ambient conditions, warm-up behavior and any temperature warning. Follow a separate overheating or red-stop warning immediately.
safety: Do not remove a cooling-system cap while the system is hot. Keep clear of fans and moving belts.
nextSteps: Provide the saved temperature-related scan information to the workshop.
Ask for the applicable diagnostic test before a cooling-system repair.

P0401.summary: P0401 identifies exhaust-gas-recirculation flow reported as insufficient by the diagnostic monitor.
P0401.meaning: The flow result does not isolate a valve, passage, sensor or control fault. Those distinctions require the exact engine’s diagnostic procedure.
P0401.firstCheck: Record the full code list and whether there is rough running or loss of power. Avoid touching hot exhaust and EGR components.
nextSteps: Provide the engine identity and the saved scan conditions.
Do not bypass the EGR system or choose a component solely from this title.

P0011.summary: P0011 reports camshaft timing over-advanced or system performance for the camshaft and bank identified in the definition.
P0011.meaning: A timing-related result needs the exact engine configuration and service procedure. It is not a direct diagnosis of a timing chain or control solenoid.
P0011.firstCheck: Record unusual engine noise, starting difficulty, warning lamps and recent service. Follow the owner manual for any oil-pressure or stop warning.
nextSteps: Give the complete code list and recent service history to the technician.
Avoid disassembly or repeated running when mechanical noise or a critical warning is present.

P0016.summary: P0016 reports a crankshaft/camshaft correlation result outside the expected relationship for the bank and sensor identified in the definition.
P0016.meaning: The reported relationship must be checked with the engine-specific procedure. The code does not establish whether the cause is sensing, control or mechanical.
P0016.firstCheck: Record hard starting, unusual noise and any recent timing or engine work. Do not repeatedly crank an engine that sounds abnormal.
nextSteps: Preserve related timing and sensor codes.
Use a qualified technician for timing-system testing.

P0A80.summary: P0A80 is a high-voltage battery-system reference. The complete scan, subcodes and exact hybrid or electric powertrain are essential to diagnosis.
P0A80.meaning: The code label is not an owner repair procedure. Battery assessment and service require appropriate high-voltage training and vehicle-specific equipment.
P0A80.firstCheck: Record the complete scan and dashboard message from a safe location. Follow any instruction to stop, and arrange qualified hybrid/EV service.
safety: Do not open the traction battery, touch high-voltage cables or attempt to isolate the high-voltage system from this guide.
Keep away from a damaged, smoking, hot or leaking traction battery and obtain emergency assistance when appropriate.
nextSteps: Use a workshop qualified for the actual high-voltage platform.
Supply all subcodes and warnings rather than only the five-character code.

U0100.summary: U0100 reports lost communication with the engine/powertrain control module identified in the generic definition.
U0100.meaning: A module named in a lost-communication code is not automatically defective. The reporting module and the rest of the network scan matter.
U0100.firstCheck: Keep all module communication results and note whether the vehicle starts. Record a recent battery failure or repair only if it actually occurred.
nextSteps: Ask for the vehicle-specific network and power-supply diagnosis.
Do not replace or program a controller based only on a communication-code title.
